content.title: Re: Official Review of Paper820 by Reviewer s97d
content.comment:
Thanks for your effort in reviewing our paper. We respond to specific comments below.
 
>Can you compare your method with more Chinese Benchmarks such as Taisu? (also in some English dataset)

Thanks for the comment. We will adopt our proposed VLP method R2D2 to more Chinese benchmarks and English datasets in future work. 
 
>The technical contribution is weak. The model architecture follows the original CLIP paper. Global Contrastive Pre-Ranking and Masked Language Modeling are not new.

The proposed framework actually consists of the model architecture, pre-training strategies, and the two-way distillation method. Different from the dual-stream model (e.g., CLIP), we combine dual-stream architecture with single-stream architecture, where the single-stream architecture consists of two cross encoders. The cross encoders are able to learn image-to-text and text-to-image interactions in a fine-grained manner. During pre-training, we design a global contrastive pre-ranking loss to obtain image-text representations and fine-grained ranking loss to further improve model performance. We apply masked language modeling with enhanced training to decrease the computational cost of pre-training. We also introduce a two-way distillation method, consisting of target-guided distillation and feature-guided distillation. The target-guided distillation increases the robustness when learning from noisy labels, while feature-guided distillation aims to improve the generalization performance. We improved masked language modeling with enhanced training. We will reorganize the text in a new version.
 
>ZERO only contains 23 million samples (smaller compared to Wukong(100M) and Taisu).

Thanks for the comment. We try to find a balance among the long-tail distribution, noise, and computing resources. The experiments in Section 4.2 prove that our 23M pre-training dataset is more high-quality compared with Wukong 100M.
 
>Can Fine-Grained Ranking learn interpretable representation? E.g. the binary task has some meaning towards the image-text pair?

Thanks for the question. We have discussed the effect of Fine-Grained Ranking (FGR) in the section of Ablation Study. The experimental results show that FGR is indeed powerful. 
 
>The two-way distillation will greatly slow down the training. Do you have a computational throughput analysis for the training?

We maintain a momentum queue and stop its gradient backward in two-way distillation. In this way, the training time of our proposed method with two-way distillation does not increase substantially.

>Can you provide the dataset link?

Due to the double-blind rule, we will release all datasets and models after the paper is accepted.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a large-scale Chinese cross-modal pre-training dataset called ZERO. For large-scale cross-modal pre-training, a framework called R2D2 is also proposed. Extensive results are provided to construct the Chinese benchmark.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ A large-scale Chinese cross-modal pre-training dataset ZERO is presented.
+ A pre-training framework R2D2 is also proposed for cross-modal learning.
+ A Chinese benchmark is constructed for cross-modal pre-training.

Weaknesses:
- This paper is closely related to WenLan which also presents a Chinese cross-modal pre-training benchmark of 650M image-text pairs. Since WenLan has been published in Nature Communications, please correctly cite it and also discuss about it in detail.
- In my opinion, it makes no sense to construct a large-scale Chinese pre-training benchmark which is filtered from 5B image-text pairs to 32M ones. In this way, the long-tailed concepts have (at a high risk) been removed from the benchmark. Note that the most important role of pre-training lies in dealing with long-tailed concepts, especially for Chinese cross-modal pre-training. Therefore, the constructed benchmark ZERO is actually not suitable for training a Chinese cross-modal pre-training model. 
- The proposed R2D2 has the same mixed architecture as ALBEF and BLIP. Please give a detailed discussion.

content.title: Re: Official Review of Paper820 by Reviewer k16p
content.comment:
Thanks for your effort in reviewing our paper. We respond to specific comments below.

>This paper is closely related to WenLan which also presents a Chinese cross-modal pre-training benchmark of 650M image-text pairs. Since WenLan has been published in Nature Communications, please correctly cite it and also discuss about it in detail.

Thanks for pointing this out. We cite the arxiv version of WenLan [1] in our original submission. We will cite the latest version [2] in our new paper.

[1] WenLan 2.0: Make AI Imagine via a Multimodal Foundation Model. arXiv preprint arXiv:2110.14378, 2021.

[2] Towards artificial general intelligence via a multimodal foundation model. Nature Communications, 13(1):1–13, 2022  
  
>In my opinion, it makes no sense to construct a large-scale Chinese pre-training benchmark which is filtered from 5B image-text pairs to 32M ones. In this way, the long-tailed concepts have (at a high risk) been removed from the benchmark. Note that the most important role of pre-training lies in dealing with long-tailed concepts, especially for Chinese cross-modal pre-training. Therefore, the constructed benchmark ZERO is actually not suitable for training a Chinese cross-modal pre-training model.

The original 5B image-text pairs are inherently noisy and require more computing resources. We agree to the point that the most important role of pre-training lies in dealing with long-tailed concepts, even if they come with more noise. We try to find a balance among the long-tail distribution, noise, and computing resources. In this sense, we construct a large-scale Chinese pre-training benchmark by filtering from 5B pairs to 23M. The key point is filtering the candidates by the highest user CTR. We obtain high-quality image-text pairs for Chinese cross-modal learning. The experiments in Section 4.2 prove that our 23M pre-training dataset is indeed high-quality.
 
>The proposed R2D2 has the same mixed architecture as ALBEF and BLIP. Please give a detailed discussion.

Thanks for the question. Please kindly note that we have given detailed discussions of ALBEF and BLIP in Related Work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors propose a large-scale Chinese cross-modal benchmark (named ZERO) with a pre-training dataset (ZERO-Corpus) and five downstream datasets. ZERO-Corpus includes 23 million image-text pairs collected from the search engine. In addition, a pre-training framework with pre-Ranking + Ranking with target-guided Distillation and feature-guided Distillation (R2D2 for short) for cross-modal learning is developed. The proposed model has been evaluated on eleven downstream datasets from four categories of tasks, including image-text retrieval, image-text matching, image caption, and text-to-image generation.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:

1. The proposed benchmark ZERO (ZERO-Corpus for pre-training and 5 datasets for downstream tasks) can be very beneficial to the research community. 

Weaknesses:

1. The technical contribution of this work is limited. The authors claim that they present a new Vision-Language framework, but the architecture is quite common. A variant of a two-stream model structure cannot be considered as "new".
2. The experimental validation and comparisons are insufficient. The authors are expected to verify the proposed model on more tasks, such as VQA, and more recent works for multi-modal learning, such as VL-T5 (Unifying Vision-and-Language Tasks via Text Generation) and OFA (OFA: Unifying Architectures, Tasks, and Modalities Through a Simple Sequence-to-Sequence Learning Framework).

content.title: Re: Official Review of Paper820 by Reviewer e23i
content.comment:
We thank Reviewer e23i for positive comments and helpful feedback on our work. We respond to specific comments below.

>How do you get the negative samples for “Fine-Grained Ranking” ?

We obtain hard negative samples by sampling in a mini-batch. Given an image in the mini-batch, we select the corresponding negative text by ranking the contrastive scores of the current batch. We choose the higher score except for the original positive text of the image. In this way, we construct one image-text negative pair for FGR. The negative images of each text are similar to the description above.
 
>This sentence makes me confused, “we feed the representations into a fully connected layer g(·) to get the predicted probabilities” . What is the form of your target probabilities? How do you get the ground-truth label of binary classification?

Given the representations $N\times768$ (where $N$ is the batch-size of image-text pairs and $768$ is the output dim of the cross encoders), we feed them into a fully connected layer. Then, the representations $N\times768$ will be projected as $N\times2$, where the second dim is the form of our predicted probabilities. The ground-truth label of positive image-text pairs is 1 while the negative pairs are 0. We compute the FGR loss via cross-entropy loss. 

We will make these constructive comments in a new version.
